01 — About

From Engineering
to Enterprise Value

I am an engineering graduate now completing an MBA in Financial Consulting at Lovely Professional University, building a career at the intersection of corporate finance, valuation and business analytics.

Before the transition, I spent a year as a Project Engineer at Kadence Automation and Robotics, helping deliver ₹11 Crore in revenue across 16 B2B client accounts — an engineering-rooted grounding in cost, ROI and capital allocation that now shapes how I approach financial analysis.

I was selected as one of 60 students nationally for the BNY Mellon Spectrum Program in Private Equity & Hedge Funds, and have since built hands-on depth in DCF valuation, M&A modelling, LBO structuring and FP&A — through academic projects, certifications, and a finance internship with the Dalmia Group. The next step: institutional finance, where rigorous analysis meets real capital decisions.

10 — Vision

Career Vision

Finance is where engineering discipline meets capital judgement — and that intersection is where I want to build my career.

Coming from an engineering background gave me a grounding in measuring what actually drives value — ROI, cost, utilization, throughput. The move into finance is a natural extension of that: applying the same rigor to capital structures, valuations and business performance, at a scale where the analysis directly informs decisions.

The long-term goal is a career in institutional finance — investment banking, private equity or corporate strategy — built on the modelling foundation already in place: DCF valuation, M&A structuring, LBO analysis and FP&A. In the near term, that means deepening expertise in valuation and business analytics while contributing to teams that make high-stakes capital decisions.
